22D.1 When faced with the alternative of battle we are not to be afraid of strong enemies.
22D.4 If an enemy city or territory will not surrender in peace, but wills to war against us, we are then to go to war against it and besieged the it.
22D.6 Heathen enemies within our own nation are to be totally destroyed.
22D.7 The kings or leaders of a conquered enemy are to be executed.
22D.10 All males of heathen nations are to be killed.
22D.11 Prisoners of war, cattle, and goods of a defeated nation are to be taken as a spoil.

precepts.text: The law of war: far-off cities that answer peace become tributaries, but of the cities of these nations save alive nothing that breatheth.
precepts.point: Genesis 15:13 is not talking about America. Judah has been here longer than four hundred years and the northern kingdom longer than six hundred, so this is not us coming up out of Babylon the great; and Israel was actually in Egypt four hundred and thirty years, free for the first thirty.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
There is a law pertaining to war: “When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it. And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.” If it will make no peace, thou shalt besiege it, smite every male with the edge of the sword, and take the women, the little ones, the cattle and the spoil unto thyself.

But that applied to cities very far off: “Thus shalt thou do unto all the cities which are very far off from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations. But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth: But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee”.

That is why at Hazor “there was not any left to breathe”, and in all the cities of those kings every man they smote with the edge of the sword, taking only the spoil and the cattle for a prey. As the Lord commanded Moses, so did Moses command Joshua, and so did Joshua; he left nothing undone.

precepts.text: Thy seed shall serve and be afflicted four hundred years and come hither again in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full; the destruction was prophesied and just.
precepts.point: Genesis 15:13 is not talking about America. Judah has been here longer than four hundred years and the northern kingdom longer than six hundred, so this is not us coming up out of Babylon the great; and Israel was actually in Egypt four hundred and thirty years, free for the first thirty.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
The Most High is not unjust in what he does. It was already prophesied to Abram: “Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years; And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.” Then: “But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.”

When Israel came back to establish the land, it was time for those nations to pay for their iniquities from way back when. The iniquity of the Amorites was full, and the destruction was prophesied and just.

Genesis 15:13 is not talking about America. Judah has been here longer than four hundred years and the northern kingdom longer than six hundred, so this is not us coming up out of Babylon the great; and Israel was actually in Egypt four hundred and thirty years, free for the first thirty.

precepts.text: The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; the sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; it shall happen again.
precepts.point: When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
“There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, save the Hivites the inhabitants of Gibeon”; that is why all of them went into destruction. There is nothing new under the sun; it shall happen again, and we are just waiting on it to unfold. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.” The nation that will not serve Israel shall perish, as those kings did that would not make peace; and the sons of them that afflicted us shall come bending unto us.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
We see the Most High setting it up right before our eyes: Israel is being made into warriors once again, so the days of Joshua can be once again when the Lord returns. “They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded.”

“The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: And the Lord shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?” The Lord shall utter his voice before his army, as he hardened the hearts of the kings so that they came against Israel in battle and were destroyed utterly. He is setting us in order before our enemies' eyes.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.”

Esau thinks the Most High is altogether such a one as himself, that the Most High looks like him and is happy with him punishing and oppressing us. He is not down for it; it is our punishment and it has to happen, but he will reprove Esau and set Israel in order before his eyes. As it was of the Lord to harden the hearts of those kings that he might destroy them utterly, so he kept silence while Esau did these things, and he will reprove him.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
“Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them”. Edom revenged himself upon Judah over and above his charge. “Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword.”

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.” Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury, by the hand of his people, as Joshua took all those kings and slew them. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end.

“And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.”

That is what Joshua did to all those kings, with no favour and none left to breathe, and it shall happen again: vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard, laid upon Edom by the hand of Israel. This is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

precepts.text: Joshua gave the land for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes.
precepts.point: The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the Lord said unto Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war.” What was commanded to Moses in Numbers, Joshua carried out: the land given for an inheritance unto Israel, tribe by tribe.

So when the Most High says “divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh”, it is only the Israelites who receive it. The other two and a half tribes had already received theirs, and now the rest of the land is divided among the rest of our people, according to their divisions by their tribes.
